content: This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the potential benefits to you outweigh the risks of side effects. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. However, this is not a comprehensive list of possible side effects. If you are in the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. Similarly, if you are in Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Precautions: Before using cidofovir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other antiviral medications (such as ganciclovir), to probenecid, or to other sulfa drugs (such as sulfamethoxazole). Additionally, disclose any other allergies you may have. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. This medication may cause changes in vision. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities that require clear vision until you are confident you can perform them safely. During pregnancy, cidofovir should only be used when absolutely necessary, as it may harm an unborn baby. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. The manufacturer advises avoiding pregnancy. To prevent pregnancy, men with female partners should use effective barrier protection (such as latex or polyurethane condoms) during all sexual activity while on treatment and for at least 90 days after stopping the medication. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk. If you have HIV, breast milk may transmit the virus. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription drugs, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Avoid taking other medications that may harm your kidneys (such as amphotericin B, foscarnet, pentamidine, vancomycin, aminoglycosides like tobramycin, or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) like ibuprofen) within seven days before and during treatment with this medication. In some cases, serious (and potentially fatal) kidney damage may occur. Check the labels on all your medications, as they may contain NSAIDs (such as ibuprofen or naproxen). Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Notes: Laboratory and/or medical tests (such as eye exams) should be conducted while you are using this medication. Keep all medical and lab appointments. To reduce the risk of spreading HIV to others, use an effective barrier method (such as latex or polyurethane condoms/dental dams) during sexual activity. Missed Dose: It is crucial to receive each dose of this medication as scheduled. If you miss a dose of cidofovir, contact your doctor or pharmacist immediately for a new dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. If you miss a dose of probenecid, inform your doctor or pharmacist right away. Storage: Consult the product instructions and your pharmacist for storage details. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This is a summary and does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Warning: This medication may cause serious (and potentially fatal) kidney problems. To prevent kidney issues, your doctor will typically prescribe another medication (probenecid) and direct you to receive intravenous fluids. Avoid other medications that may also harm your kidneys (refer to the Drug Interactions section). This medication can reduce the body’s ability to fight infections. Laboratory and/or medical tests (such as kidney function and complete blood counts) should be performed before each dose to monitor for these side effects. Consult your doctor for more details. Cidofovir has caused tumors in laboratory animals. Although there is no information regarding humans, cidofovir should be considered potentially carcinogenic (cancer-causing). Uses: This drug is used in combination with probenecid to treat a specific viral eye infection (retinitis caused by cytomegalovirus CMV) in individuals with AIDS. It reduces the risk of blindness and other vision problems. Cidofovir belongs to a class of drugs known as antivirals. How to Use: This medication is administered by injection into a vein as directed by your doctor, usually every one to two weeks. It is injected slowly into a vein over one hour. This medication should not be injected into the eyes. The dosage is based on your medical condition, body weight, and response to treatment. You will typically receive intravenous fluids before your dose of cidofovir. Your doctor will also instruct you to take probenecid orally before and after receiving cidofovir. To prevent kidney problems, drink plenty of fluids unless otherwise directed by your doctor. If you are administering this medication at home, learn all preparation and usage instructions from your healthcare professional. Before use, visually inspect this product for particles or discoloration. If either is present, do not use the liquid. It is essential to use probenecid with this medication exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Nausea and vomiting caused by probenecid may be prevented by taking it after meals. This medication works best when used regularly. Keep all your medical appointments. Do not use more or less of this drug than prescribed or stop using it (or your HIV medications) even for a short time unless directed by your doctor. Avoid direct contact of this medication with the skin, eyes, or mouth. If contact occurs, wash thoroughly with soap and water. Nausea may occur. Headache, nausea, and vomiting may also occur with probenecid use.
